new_statements.quote: A measure is a unit of speech of not more than three syllables, that has one stressed syllable. It may consist of a single long syllable, e.g. kwā, mē, kwai, vou, of two or three short syllables, e.g. ciwa, vatu, alewa, tamata, na vatu, or of a short syllable plus a long syllable, e.g. cavā, rogō, tubā, vecē, na kai. Stress falls on any long syllable and on the penultimate syllable of a measure consisting of short syllables, e.g. ciwa, noa, vatu, tamata, alewa or on the final syllable of a measure that ends in a long syllable, e.g. tarā, kwadrē. A sequence of two long syllables, e.g. rātū, vōvō, consists of two measures because each syllable is stressed.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Fijian-type measure-based (moraic-trochee) stress: every long syllable (long vowel, diphthong ai/au/ei/eu/iu/oi/ou, or long m̄) is stressed; in a measure of short syllables stress is penultimate; a measure ending in a long syllable is stressed on that final long syllable. Equivalent to stress on the syllable containing the penultimate mora of each measure; words of several measures carry one stress per measure. A long syllable may not precede a short one within a measure (underlying long vowels shorten before a cliticised short syllable, vū + ni kai -> vunikai).
new_statements.secondary_stress: No primary/secondary ranking within the word is stated; each measure of a multi-measure word carries its own stress (e.g. kivi+laki+nia, vaka+tunu+loa). At phrase level one syllable per intonation contour carries a more prominent 'phrase stress' (louder and/or higher-pitched).
new_statements.exceptions: Diphthongs ai, au, ei, eu, iu, oi, ou count as single long (stressed) syllables while ea, ia, oa, ua, ie, ue are two short syllables; short monosyllabic object/possessive clitics (-a, -ru, -ra, focus marker) attach as unstressed syllables and trigger shortening of a preceding long vowel; polysyllabic or long pronouns carry their own stress. Geraghty 1979 (sec. 3.9) adds a Western-Fijian-wide phrase-level lengthening of phrase-antepenultimate a.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the measure (prosodic foot of at most three syllables), not the orthographic word; orthographic words may contain several measures each with a stress; phrase stress is a separate, higher level. Examples are citation forms from the dictionary.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Wayan dialect (Waya and Viwa islands, southern Yasawas; Glottolog waya1268), one of three Glottolog dialects of west2519 (the others: Nadrogaa nadr1235, Northwest Viti Levu nucl1487). Pawley & Sayaba treat all Western Fijian communalects as one internally diverse language. Geraghty 1979 secs 3.9-3.10 add that all Western communalects (Waya, Nakoroboya, Magodro, Tubai, etc.) share phrase-antepenultimate a-lengthening and stress the first vowel of low/mid-to-high vowel sequences, on top of the pan-Fijian (measure-)penultimate stress rule. Geraghty 2002 (not opened) describes the Nadrogaa dialect.

sources.note: Sec. 3.2 'Measures and stress' (footer p. 15, PDF p. 18): stress falls on any long syllable and on the penultimate syllable of a measure of short syllables, or on the final syllable of a measure ending in a long syllable; two long syllables = two measures each stressed; long+short measure disallowed (long vowel shortens before cliticised short syllable); phrase stress = one more prominent (louder/higher) syllable per intonation contour.

sources.citation: Geraghty, Paul A. 1979. Topics in Fijian language history. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii (published revised as Geraghty 1983, The History of the Fijian Languages, Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 19). hdl:10125/76152
sources.note: Assumes the pan-Fijian (measure-)penultimate stress rule (citing Schutz 1976); sec. 3.9: all Western communalects have phrase-level lengthening of phrase-antepenultimate a (probably an intonation peak); sec. 3.10: in all Fijian languages except Lau the penultimate rule is qualified so that stress always falls on the first vowel of a low/mid-to-high vowel sequence (NWN raica vs LAU raica); fn: suffixation by a bisyllabic form does not affect stress assignment in the base.
